claims.text: The starting feedstock is AlCrFeNiSi powder with a controlled, narrow particle-size distribution produced by gas atomization.
The proposed intervention is a uniform 50–60 nm ALD-deposited Al2O3 coating on the AlCrFeNiSi powder.
An ultrathin Al2O3 coating will moderate heat transfer during laser-based additive manufacturing.
The Al2O3 coating forms engineered particle–matrix interfaces that act as thermally robust barriers.
The coated interfaces influence solidification behavior so as to produce a fine microstructure.
The Al2O3 coating smooths heat flux into individual powder particles during laser melting.
Moderated thermal input reduces steep thermal gradients.
Reduced thermal gradients reduce the development of residual stress.
The moderated thermal input fosters rapid solidification and microstructural refinement.
Optimization of coating conditions can preserve metallurgical bonding and prevent interfacial weakness.
The applicable geometry is miniature components with feature sizes of approximately 1–2 mm.
Fabrication is to occur in an inert atmosphere on a conventional laser-based system operated at reduced overall power.
Coated-powder components will have significantly lower residual stresses than components made from uncoated powder under conventional high-thermal-load processing.
Coated-powder components will exhibit a more refined microstructure than the high-thermal-load uncoated baseline.
Coated-powder components will exhibit enhanced hardness relative to the high-thermal-load uncoated baseline.
Coated-powder components will exhibit improved tensile performance relative to the high-thermal-load uncoated baseline.
XRD and microindentation can be used to map residual stress in the fabricated components.
The precise optimal coating thickness and surface chemistry required to maintain robust metallurgical bonding are uncertain.
The long-term reliability effects and scalability of the ALD coating process are not established.

contradictions.description: The 50–60 nm coating is described as optimized and the experiment calls for optimized coating parameters, while the uncertainty field states that the precise optimal thickness and surface chemistry are unknown.

The main prediction compares coated material processed at reduced power with an uncoated high-thermal-load baseline, whereas the falsification experiment and rule compare coated and uncoated powders under matched laser conditions. These are different operational comparisons, so the proposed test does not directly falsify the stated reduced-power-versus-high-load prediction.
